findings.reason: a worker told to judge the bounds against a store that no longer exists will either hunt for it or measure something else, and the "store removed" reference pass becomes unstateable.
findings.text: §42's Deliverable says the bounds are "judged on the corpus as copied, with the crew home's git-answer store as production left it" and asks for "one pass per storage with that store removed", but the git-answer store was created by the earlier §41 ("a store under the crew home keyed by head sha and base sha"); the retargeted §41 now reads the head from git's files and builds no store, and no other section (§40, §43) creates one

findings.reason: an absence claim needs a check shown to see known-present calls, and without a declared control the node cannot distinguish a real zero from a dead recorder.
findings.text: §40's done-when requires "the per-call-site table at both revisions, with calls per derivation and seconds, and names the call sites that grew" but declares no sentinel or negative control, so an instrument that records nothing satisfies it vacuously; the census's own headline result is the absence claim "Sites that grew: none"

findings.reason: on the plan's own census numbers §41+§43 leave the first `fleet_state` several seconds over the 10 s bound, so the route to closing §34's bounds is incomplete and a repair section for the remaining git sites is missing.
findings.text: §42's Why says "With git cached, it projected 11.0 to 11.5 s" and concludes the re-measurement needs only §41 and §43, but the census's 11.0–11.5 s is explicitly "with every call answered from cache" (24.1–26.4 s measured minus all 13.0–15.2 s of child wait), while §41 removes only `_reviewed_run_head`'s ~7.3–8.1 s of the ~14.1 s a derivation pays; `_resolve_commit` (2.4–2.9 s, the census's one object-id-only site) and the first derivation's `git rev-list` (~3.7 s, cold per-process cache) remain uncached and no section picks them up

findings.reason: as written §41 reads as blocked on an unfinished §40, so a coordinator will withhold a node whose evidence has in fact landed, and the state contradicts the content the same edit added.
findings.text: `_document` still declares `s40` implementable and f-araiid-029 is open saying "The census ... dispatched as run r-20261018T201144142528", while §41 declares `depends-on` §40 and §41–§43's Whys cite that census as completed evidence; the run record shows `status: complete`, job 1289493, every census log EXIT=0

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §42's Deliverable judges the bounds against "the crew home's git-answer store", and no section creates that store since §41 was retargeted.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §40's done-when names no instrument control or negative control although its whole deliverable is an absence claim ("names the call sites that grew").
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §40, §41 and §42 write to the run's report directory and §41's and §43's logs sit under the run directory; none names a session scratchpad or a node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test filenames and the named symbols describe the mechanism (`test_a_review_row_reads_its_head_from_files.py`, `test_a_derivation_builds_the_ledger_index_once.py`) and carry no plan label, ticket number or version tag.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §42's Why reads the census's "every call answered from cache" projection as the result §41 delivers, but §41 removes one of the four git call sites, so the arithmetic behind the stated route to closure is short by roughly 6 s.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §40 carries one census, §41 one head-resolution change, §42 one re-measurement and §43 one index-sharing change, each closeable on a single verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §41 declares `depends-on` §40 and §41–§43's Whys cite §40's census as completed evidence, yet `_document` still declares `s40` implementable and leaves f-araiid-029 open describing the census as merely dispatched.
